newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices slightly softer.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices slightly softer.

text.p: U.S. Municipal bonds opened slightly softer Friday as U.S. dollar woes helped pulled U.S. Treasuries sharply lower.
One trader said muni cash was a basis point weaker on the bid side.
"The dollar I think is pulling down the bond market a little bit," he said. "It's very thin trading so it's a little whippy in here this morning, but (it is) very quiet in munis."

The benchmark 30-year bond was down 25/32 at 96-30/32 to yield 6.61 percent. In debt futures, the September municipal contract was down 19/32 at 119-6/32. The September T-bond contract was down 20/32 at 113. The MOB spread was 198 ticks.
A second trader said inactivity made it difficult to peg muni cash levels.
"There's nothing going on," the trader said, adding that next week is likely to be dead as well.
"It's a big vacation time," he said. "There's not a lot of new issues, it's just going to be more of the same."

Next week's new issues are expected to number 93 and total $1.8 billion. Competitive deals are expected to number 58 and total $684 million, while negotiated deals are expected to total 35 and total $1.149 billion.
In the note market, Texas is expected to offer $2.9 billion of tax and revenue anticipation notes for bids on August 27. The non-callable notes, are dated September 2, 1997 and due Aug. 31, 1998.
